Bassist Steve Gilmore was born in Trenton, NJ on January 21, 1943. He was working professionally while still in his teens, attended Oscar Peterson’s Advanced School of Contemporary Music and gained experience with Ira Sullivan and Flip Phillips while living in Florida. Steve freelanced in the northeast in the seventies, performing with the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis Orchestra, Mose Allison and Toshiko Akiyoshi. Since 1974 he has been an integral part of the Phil Woods Quartet, touring steadily and participating in the recording of numerous critically-acclaimed albums. He also finds time to tour with artists such as guitarist Jim Hall and vocalist Carol Sloane.
Steve was interviewed in Delaware Water Gap, PA on November 8, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. My name is Monk Rowe and we are in Delaware Water Gap at the Deerhead Inn. I’m pleased to have bassist Steve Gilmore with me. It’s a pleasure to meet you, and perhaps talk about why would you choose to make a living as a jazz musician? But we can save that — I mean that’s a big subject.
